name: Sputnik 1 orbital satellite
description: A Soviet artificial satellite orbited Earth and broadcast radio signals in 1957.

impact.note: First orbital launch; the Soviet space line descended from it, but other countries' satellites came from programmes already under way, so not scored as the platform.

date.basis: The cited source dates this scoped episode.

events.statement: The Soviet Union placed Sputnik 1 in Earth orbit; its radio transmitters sent signals receivable on Earth.
events.caveats: The announcement reflects early reported parameters. The satellite is one achievement, not a claim about all rocketry.

evidence.supports: NASA dates launch; translated TASS statement describes orbit and transmission.
Identifies Sputnik’s launch site as Baikonur in Soviet Kazakhstan.

events.place_note: Country-level place denotes launch site, not the satellite’s orbital path.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in the cited passages for this scoped referent; no global priority beyond the event is assumed.

caveats: Earlier sounding rockets reached space without entering Earth orbit; the source is an official contemporary announcement with a NASA headnote.

measures.subject: Sputnik 1
measures.conditions: Mass reported in the contemporaneous TASS statement.

research.note: Independent reader checked the named reviewed facets against the cited documents; no global priority or unreported funding inferred.

places.note: Launch from Baikonur, then in the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic; the flight was in Earth orbit.
